Line Integrals with Respect to dx, dy, or dz

When analyzing forces or flows, it is often useful to consider each component direction separately. In such situations we want a line integral of a scalar function with respect to one of the coordinates, such as 1C M dx. This integral is not the same as the arc length line integral 1C M ds we defined in Section 16.1. To define the integral 1C M dx for the scalar function M(x, y, z), we specify a vector field F = M(x, y, z)i having a component only in the x-direction, and none in the y- or z-direction. Then, over the curve C parametrized by r(t) = g(t)i + h(t)j + k(t)k for a … t … b, we have x = g(t), dx = g′(t) dt, and
